# Generator Assumptions — Cascadia Deal Desk

*Auto-generated by `src/generate.py`. Seed **20260801**, as-of **2026-08-01**, window **2024-08-01 → 2026-07-31**.*

> **Synthetic data, seeded generator. Simulated — not real company data.** There is no real pricing data in this project. Every customer, part number, price and person below was invented by this script from a fixed seed. Any resemblance to a real company, product or individual is unintended.

## Why the variance is generated, not drawn

The obvious way to build this dataset would be to draw the quoted price from
a distribution around the agreed price. That produces directionless noise: an
exception table with no story and a threshold control that does nothing when
you drag it. So variance here comes from a **mechanism** instead.

Every customer/product relationship carries a `prior_price` — what that
customer paid before the current agreement. When an agreement is signed the
`agreed_price` sits at a **premium** above it. An off-agreement line is a rep
quoting the *prior* price: the old number, from habit or from a stale sheet.

That one mechanism gives the analysis three properties for free:

- variance is **negative** (undercharging), because the premium was positive;
- variance is **larger where the premium was larger**, because it *is* the premium;
- variance is **explainable**, because the counterfactual is a real column in the data.

Jitter (a rounded number, a slightly stale sheet) sits on top, and is
deliberately second-order. It is never the driver.

## Realized mix (this run)

| Outcome | Lines | Share of all lines | Design band |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Priced to agreement | 2,316 | 77.1% | 80–85% *of covered lines* |
| Priced off agreement | 426 | 14.2% | 13–16% of all lines |
| No governing agreement | 261 | 8.7% | 8–10% of all lines |

Of the **2,742** lines that have a governing agreement, **84.5%** are priced to it. A dataset where everything is broken is not credible and would undercut the argument.

Approved exceptions: **48** lines, **11.3%** of off-agreement lines (design target ~12%). These are documented, approved deviations — without them there are no false positives to calibrate against and the threshold control on the exception page is theatre.

## Parameter block

Every tunable assumption in the dataset, as it was set for this run.

| Parameter | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `SEED` | 20260801 | Fixed seed; the same seed reproduces byte-identical CSVs |
| `N_CUSTOMERS` / `N_PRODUCTS` / `N_REPS` | 40 / 120 / 12 | Size of the book |
| `TARGET_QUOTE_LINES` | 3,000 | Approximate line count (quotes carry 1–4 lines) |
| `TOLERANCE_PCT` | ±0.5% | Band inside which a quote counts as priced *to* the agreement |
| `PREMIUM_NORMAL` / `PREMIUM_HARD` | (0.03, 0.15) / (0.15, 0.3) | The uplift a renegotiation won over `prior_price` |
| `PREMIUM_HARD_SHARE` | 20% | Share of agreements negotiated hard |
| `BASE_OFF_AGREEMENT_RATE` | 0.044 | Baseline P(off-agreement) before the three drivers |
| `REP_LEAK_STANDOUT` | 4.0× | The one rep who is the story |
| `N_LEAKY_REPS` | 4 of 12 | Reps carrying the clear majority of leakage |
| `RECENCY_PEAK_BOOST` / `RECENCY_DECAY_DAYS` | 3.0× / 45d | Leakage peaks just after a renegotiation, then decays |
| `N_HOT_CUSTOMERS` | 6 | Accounts carrying most of the dollar exposure |
| `EXCEPTION_BASE_RATE` | 0.013 | Rate of documented, approved deviations |
| `P_EXCEPTION_POSITIVE` | 35% | Approved deviations priced *above* agreement |
| `CHAIN_LENGTH_WEIGHTS` | {1: 0.7, 2: 0.22, 3: 0.08} | How often a customer/part relationship renews |
| `SUCCESSOR_OVERLAP_P` | 30% | Successors back-dated into the predecessor's window |
| `N_UNLINKED_OVERLAPS` | 9 | Duplicate registrations with no supersession link |
| `COST_DRIFT_MIX` (down/flat/up) | (0.45, 0.35, 0.2) | Standard-cost trajectory per part |
| `CONVERSION_BY_SEGMENT` | {'Strategic': 0.66, 'Core': 0.6, 'Emerging': 0.52} | Quote → booking conversion |
| `YOY_GROWTH` | 17.5% | Year-2 quote volume vs year-1 |

## Structures built on purpose

A reader is entitled to know which findings were designed in rather than
discovered. All of these are deliberate:

- **6 concentrated accounts** and **4 undisciplined reps** (one standout), so the ranked-by-dollars charts have a genuine head and tail.
- **4 margin-erosion accounts** — near-perfect compliance, but their parts carry *rising* standard cost. These produce the second, separate finding: the agreement was honoured and the margin still fell. That is a different failure from leakage and the data has to be able to tell them apart.
- **3 strategic accounts** where approved deviations cluster, some of them priced *above* the agreement.
- **9 duplicate registrations** with no supersession link — the case the recency tiebreak exists for.
- **8 parts that launch mid-window**, creating genuine `product_launched_after_agreement` coverage gaps.
